subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Erie Canal: Digging Prosperity
description: A quick, practical guide to The Erie Canal: Digging Prosperity.

hook.text: In 1817, shipping goods from Buffalo to New York cost $100 per ton. The Erie Canal cut it to $4.

buildup.text: The canal stretched 584 kilometers through forests and swamps. Workers dug it by hand in 8 years.

discovery.text: Engineers solved a 170-meter elevation change with 83 locks — staircase-like chambers that raise boats.

twist.text: Not a single trained engineer worked on the project. Self-taught Americans figured it out as they went.

climax.text: The canal made New York City the nation's commercial capital. Without it, that title might be Philadelphia's.

punchline.text: A ditch made New York the center of America.

quiz.question: What made the Erie Canal engineering project unusual?
options: It was built entirely by convict labor over two decades
No trained engineers worked on it — self-taught Americans built it
It was the first canal to use concrete-lined channels
